title: Extension Allowances and Patient Notice Points by Referral Type
content:
Referrals & Prior Authorizations types differ in how often a case may be extended, the figures an extension works with, and the points at which the patient is contacted about a referral running out.

## Extension figures

| Referral type | Most extensions per referral | Extension units | Extension validity days (calendar) | Extension request lead (calendar days) | Re-evaluation visit completed before an extension is requested |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| In-Group Specialist Referral | 2 | 4 | 90 | 14 | No |
| HMO Specialist Referral | 1 | 3 | 90 | 10 | No |
| Standing Specialist Referral | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | No |
| Out-of-Network Referral | 1 | 2 | 60 | 10 | No |
| Physical Therapy Episode Authorization | 2 | 8 | 30 | 7 | Yes |
| Advanced Imaging Prior Authorization | 1 | 0 | 30 | 5 | No |
| Outpatient Procedure Prior Authorization | 1 | 0 | 30 | 5 | No |

- **Extension units** are the units one extension adds; 0 means an extension adds validity only.
- **Extension validity days** are the tier's figure, in calendar days, for validity an extension adds to the valid-through date.
- **Extension request lead** is the number of calendar days before the valid-through date (or before the last unit is used) by which the coordinator asks for an extension so care is not interrupted.
- **Most extensions per referral** of 0 means the type receives no extension.

## Patient notice points

| Referral type | Expiry notice (calendar days before the valid-through date) | Nearly-used-up notice (units remaining) | Contact when no visit booked (calendar days after approval) |
|---|---|---|---|
| In-Group Specialist Referral | 14 | 2 | 14 |
| HMO Specialist Referral | 14 | 1 | 14 |
| Standing Specialist Referral | 30 | 3 | 30 |
| Out-of-Network Referral | 14 | 1 | 14 |
| Physical Therapy Episode Authorization | 7 | 3 | 10 |
| Advanced Imaging Prior Authorization | 7 | 0 (no notice) | 7 |
| Outpatient Procedure Prior Authorization | 7 | 0 (no notice) | 14 |

- The **expiry notice** tells the patient the referral is about to expire.
- The **nearly-used-up notice** is given when the units remaining reach the figure shown; 0 means no such notice.
- The **no-visit contact** is made by the coordinator to a patient who has not booked a visit that many calendar days after approval.

## Illustrations (hypothetical cases)

- An In-Group Specialist Referral with 2 units remaining has reached its nearly-used-up figure; with 3 remaining it has not.
- An Advanced Imaging Prior Authorization never produces a nearly-used-up notice, because its figure is 0.
